    Hear from Eon at Tūpore Infrastructure Limited as he talks us through the completed Kererū Road rebuild. This $5 million Cyclone Gabrielle recovery project has rebuilt five kilometres of road, delivering a safer, more resilient route for the Kererū community that will serve locals for decades to come. Funded through the Government's cyclone recovery programme via the National Infrastructure Funding and Financing (NIFF).

    A major Cyclone Gabrielle recovery rebuild of Kererū Road has now been completed, delivering a safer, more resilient road designed to serve the community for decades to come. Since October last year, work has been underway rebuilding four sections across about five kilometres of the road starting from Maraekākaho village, that suffered significant damage from the cyclone and subsequent weather events. Throughout the project, council and contractors worked closely with the community to minimise disruption and refine how the road performs, particularly around safety near the school, drainage, and making subtle improvements. Community input was very important to address concerns and adjust the design as needed. The $5 million project was funded through the Government's cyclone recovery programme via the National Infrastructure Funding and Financing (NIFF). Read more: https://lnkd.in/eYSkhe6d

    A big day for Flaxmere! The opening of the new Woolworths supermarket this morning is fantastic news for the community, bringing choice, convenience, local jobs and investment to one of Hastings' fastest-growing suburbs. The place has been buzzing as residents take the opportunity to check it out and do some shopping. It's an important milestone in the wider revitalisation of Flaxmere, with new homes and improved public spaces, and the redevelopment of the town centre to come. Council's role has been to provide the infrastructure, and to work with development partners who are funding the homes and commercial buildings. This is more than a new supermarket. It's a sign of confidence in Flaxmere's future. It's Flaxmere's time.

    Take a closer look at the Mangarau 2c flood resilience project. Stage 1 is now complete, with upgrades at Joll and Plassey, new access ramps, and improvements to pipes and sumps along Joll Road to help move rainwater and reduce flooding. Work is now moving into the next stages, including stream widening, bank strengthening, pipe upgrades and lifting two bridges. Watch the video to see the progress so far and what’s happening next around Tanner Street.
